188.t: Taking up banjo and joining the steamer Capitol

190.t: Riverboat work and Piron's society band
190.s: He played on the Capitol riverboat for years with Piron, whose society band read music and used Purple Rose of Cairo as its theme.

190.t: Dejan's Dixie boat band and drummer Judge; request to play
190.s: Dejan tells how Judge got on the Dixie boat band, then Purnell is asked to play a piece and agrees.
190.q: He likes it, too. Yeah. They bass, too, you know. Yeah. Just a couple of more minutes on here. You wanted to hear Pedro play a piece. If it feels like it... It's not a Sunday style. How you feel like it? Yeah, I guess I can.

280.t: The Lake Michigan excursion boats and the drummer Tom
280.s: He played on the North Shore excursion boat. The pay was a dollar plus $16-17 a night in tips. Tom, a New Orleans musician, later quit for the steel mill.
280.q: Yeah. On a boat. Didn't get no pay there. No? No. Just tip. They give you one dollar to come down for coffee. Oh. And, well, as it rained the boat didn't go out. It was a boat go out in the lake and come back. You know, go to Jackson Park out there from downtown and come back. Oh, yeah. They had…

280.t: How the dance boats worked and what they paid
280.s: He explains the boats ran a quarter-a-dance cruise from downtown to Jackson Park, and the band played hard to draw people on, earning $16-17 a night.
280.q: They had two boats, they had two boats out there, you know. Oh, yeah. They had two boats. They hadn't seen the North Shore, I was on the North Shore. There was boats just go up to the lake and dance, they play a quarter, like a, like a Jitney dance, like a Texan dance. You play a quarter and dance…

876.t: Sitting in at Jazzland and getting music first on the boat
876.s: He and Pops Foster sat in at an open-air club and handled a trick tune change, because the boat got new music before others.
876.q: Well, yes. I went there and sit in with the band one night. Turpin had given a macaroni dinner for the Bullock band. And we went on out there. And the guys in the band, at least a piano player in the band, he was rated as the best blues player in St. Louis. I just remember his name. I think his…

876.t: Living on the boat versus rooms ashore
876.s: The early seasons were New Orleans in winter and St. Louis in summer with rooms in town; tramp trips later forced the band to live aboard.
876.q: No, we had room ears. See that, when I left the boat, they had began to making tramp trips. You had to live on the boat.

283.t: Playing on the Capitol riverboat and as a teen
283.s: He played the Capitol with Almerico and as a teen on the boat with Fate Marable and others.
283.ch: Return to New Orleans and Sharkey
283.q: Fade Marble. And the extra band, uh, that, uh, it used to be that, uh, you had a club and you'd hire, you know, extra bands to play that. And then, uh, it would be continuous dancing. That's when I was a kid.

283.s: He worked briefly with Almerico on the steamer and recalls him fondly, paying for meals and visiting the Dream Room.
283.ch: Return to New Orleans and Sharkey
283.q: Well, they were on the steaming capitol on the... well I worked with different bands, you know? Mm-hmm. In fact, when I came back from Hollywood, I worked with Tony Amarica about two or three weeks, you know, on the boat with him.

778.t: Years on the Steamer Madison pleasure boat on Lake Pontchartrain
778.s: Contract with the Madison from West End to Mandeville and Madisonville; owners, passengers, schedule, weather and where the band played.
778.q: Me, you, the four pieces I think it was. Men, my chef on piano, and I played trumpet bass. I played with so many. You know what I mean? It's hard to keep it straight. It's hard to keep it straight. You know I played with so many of them. And sometimes you know you'll have one playing tonight and…

778.t: Nine years on the Madison, no band union, then nursing training and Detroit
778.s: Nine years on the Madison plus extra jobs, then she left for nursing in Chicago and played in Detroit.
778.q: The Camellia. I don't think that's the name of the South Camellia. I might have heard but I don't know. I never did play on it I know. No?

127.t: Fate Marble's riverboat band and Steve Lewis
127.s: Punch says he took Steve Lewis's place in Fate Marble's band on the riverboats around 1921; they try to identify the big trumpeter in the band.
127.ch: Musicians he knew and played with
127.q: Did you ever, did you know Fate Marble? No. Did you ever play the riverboat? We were on the boat, from the other St. Louis. You played with Fate Marble on the riverboat. Yes, sir. Alright, now who else was in that group? Well, I know Fate was in it. See, every time I get into something like that,…

127.t: River boats and the Charlie Taylor show
127.s: His single riverboat trip, and a Charlie Taylor show playing a boat in Wisconsin.
127.q: Taylor, one thing I can say, we did Oz with a show by the name of Charlie Taylor. We got in some town up in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and we was off, and some man hired the band, you know, and we played on the boat all night's after night.

290.t: Boxing matches and the Streckfus steamer program
290.s: He never played boxing matches; the boat had planned programs.
290.q: They had the ones who had that thing in charge. Yeah, well, Vern is still alive. One of them was a violin player I made was a fan.

290.t: The Capitol boat: a strict reading band
290.s: His one night on the Capitol was a reading band using stock arrangements; only three or four bands he knew had special arrangements.
290.ch: Sam Morgan, repertoire and Silver Leaf
290.q: Oh, it was fine. I think it was nice to work on her, you know. But it wasn't so nice for me, because that was my first night and only night there, you see. You know, I feel a little skeptical about these things.

84.t: Return to New Orleans, the Hummingbird and the Streckfus riverboat offer
84.s: Called home by his wife's operation, he works at the entertainers' club and Hummingbird and turns down the Streckfus boat job.
84.q: Then I stayed with Toody Harris about a year. Eight months a year. I got a telegram that my wife fixed to be operated on on a Saturday. And I got the telegram that Friday evening. And that's when I left that Friday evening. Come here. And uh... That Monday I went to work at the humming board. No, I…

84.t: Fate Marable guest spot and the move to St. Louis
84.s: He guested with Fate Marable on the boat, then took a $115-a-week job in St. Louis.
84.q: Walked out. We got the manager, the guy was giving the dance. He seemed, he claimed he's trying to trace him, but he never did. He didn't care about it. He didn't care about it. I think it's that. Mm-hmm. I'll take it. Yeah, he never did. He didn't care about it. Jim had to buy him another one.…

74.t: Season on the steamer St. Paul and picking up Stuff Smith
74.s: They play the whole season on the St. Paul, with Stuff Smith picked up in Ohio and Swazey back.
74.ch: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east

74.q: No; I've got that written down. We were on the steamer, St. Paul, in '28.

125.t: St. Louis and Kansas City band scenes compared
125.s: He met musicians in St. Louis, names Fate Marable, and says St. Louis bands were polished stock-arrangement outfits while Kansas City had hip nightlife.
125.ch: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands

125.t: Offer from a bandleader in St. Louis and the DeShon band
125.s: A band leader offered him a place in St. Louis after quarrelling with his pianist Cecil Scott; St. Louis and Kansas City were jazz meccas, and he played briefly with a creole bandleader.

125.q: And of course the musicians who played music were fortunate enough to make a little money, have fun. 79.t: Monday-night riverboat dances; jumping onto the boat
79.s: Monday night was the night Black patrons could go on the boats. Thomas and friends jumped onto a departing boat to hear Creath, Fate Marable's band and Zutty Singleton.

79.q: He worked for Circus Land and Fate Movable had the other gig ... I think might have been the first time I saw Zooty. And we were so anxious to hear those guys after we'd cut our lawns and did all these kind of things. Monday night was the night that's allowed for Negroes to make it.

79.s: Invited to a jam session, Thomas got a call to play with Charlie Creath at an East St. Louis gig with his new initialed cornet. Creath told him he might be a trumpet player at 25.
79.ch: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
79.q: Let me tell you about Charlie Creath. I'm going to get back to Shorty Baker, too. This is my boy, you know. So, we sat down one night -- about 5, 6 trumpet players, just a country boy, hmmm. Only tune I knew was a couple of tunes but I didn't do it on my own. I was invited. And it do make a an a…

242.t: Captain bans individual practice; four years with Pichon
242.s: Deckhands complained, so the captain limited practice to the morning band rehearsal; he stayed with Pichon four years.

175.t: Cousin Dejean; leaving on the Capitol with Desvigne in 1936
175.s: Fused exchanges about Harold Dejean, then Justin leaves New Orleans on the steamer Capitol with Sidney Desvigne, falls ill in St. Paul and settles in Chicago.

245.t: Relief band on the Streckfus steamer
245.s: His band alternated hour on, hour off with the boat band; he declined to join and played only local excursions.
245.q: Yeah, he sent him to my house to try to get me to play, join the band, you know. Well, I didn't want to quit my band, you know. Go play on the boat.

259.t: Kid Island's band, Mexico job and Fate Marable
259.s: Vincent played about two years with Kid Island, went to Mexico, and describes Fate Marable's boat band breaking up and Jimmy Dave taking the job.

904.t: Young Tuxedo Band and the Island Queen riverboat

860.t: Christie Brothers Stompers and back to sea
860.s: After Crane River split, Colyer joined the Christie Brothers Stompers for six to eight months, then rejoined the merchant navy and took a ship trading from Mobile.

622.t: Summer boat and resort jobs; Lake Delavan and Fritz Nielsen
622.s: They mention Lake Michigan boats, Delavan, Wisconsin, and the amateur pianist Fritz Nielsen.
622.q: They also played at Lake Delavan. In Wisconsin. Well, Condon and McPartland. Oh, yes. And a wonderful amateur. We always thought of him as an amateur, Fritz Nielsen, a pianist. It's probable that Fritz was the best of the Chicago pianists.

249.t: Baby Dodds and the Imperial method

429.t: Mayor's riverboat cruise, 1924, and politicians aboard

33.t: Arguing with Captain Streckfus over music on the steamer
33.s: DeDroit tells how he refused to change his New Orleans style for Captain Streckfus on the boat and left, and mentions his $500-a-night fee and Dutch Andrews.

34.s: Pasley recalls a book with old New Orleans musicians and says he played on a riverboat with Dewey Jackson of St. Louis, leaving New Orleans with him.

The most, the most, the most, the most job we, we, we, we, we, you know, we do, most of the white, you see. Most white people. I…

752.t: Pops on playing with Roppolo on the boat in 1921
752.s: Pops says he played with a clarinetist-guitarist on the riverboat in 1921.

297.t: Country parades and playing excursions upriver with Kid Rene
297.s: Farm parades up the river; New Orleans bands came for excursions, and Summers played there with Kid Rene and Chic in 1925.

621.t: Piron at Antoine's and Sidney Desvigne
621.s: Piron played nightly at Antoine's; talk of Desvigne and the riverboat trips.
621.ch: Early life and New Orleans bands
621.q: I remember Piron, I saw that job. Piron, yeah. Red Sydney, you remember Sydney? Yeah, yeah. We used to laugh at Sydney. He used to cut off. He used to cut off. Remember we used to laugh at him? Yeah, I remember.

251.t: Riverboats: the President, Susquehanna and Bill Phillips
251.s: Albert played the President only one night and other boats such as the Susquehanna on Lake Pontchartrain with Bigfoot Bill Phillips; riverboats were never a sustained job.
251.q: We worked, but only one night. A lot of people connect me with going up and down the river as a sustained thing, but I didn't.

571.t: Lake ferries between New Orleans and Mandeville
571.s: George and the interviewers recall the steamboats Camellia, Fairhope and Susquehanna, with Raymond Burke playing on one.
571.ch: Lake boats and brass band practice

12.t: Fate Marable's calliope and the quiet New Orleans night
12.s: He explains the steam calliope on Marable's riverboat, heard across the quiet city at nine o'clock.
12.q: No, no, the band stays on the boat. He's playing this thing on the boat, by the river on Canal Street, on the head of Canal Street. And these sounds would go all over, you know what I mean? The city was quiet.

482.t: Red Cayou and Fate Marable on the riverboat
482.s: Walter Lewis recalls that Red Cayou and Fate Marable worked on the steamer Capitol, and that it was mostly band work with some solos.

918.t: Band photograph, calliope tunes and the river trip

286.s: Russ played with the Silver Top band five or six years; he declined Fate Marable's riverboat to stay near family, then moved to another band.

847.t: Arrangements, Sidney as a boss, and the riverboat
847.s: The band used stocks and Joe Phillips arrangements; Sidney was a fine boss; Jackson joined after the band left the boat.

288.t: Fate Marable's riverboat bands; working until 1925 and then insurance
288.s: He played as extra with Marable's boat bands but declined a regular spot, and after his 1925 illness sold insurance until 1940.
288.ch: Maple Leaf, own orchestra and rivals
288.q: I played with Maitway. Oh I see. Whenever he had, you know, next year, then we played out, the band played on there too, the Silver Deef band.

633.t: Robichaux band and Susquehanna lake excursion boat

192.t: Sidney Desvigne's band and the steamer Capitol

291.t: Playing the Island Queen and taxi dance halls
291.s: He never played river boats except the Island Queen in New Orleans, and he notes that he never saw Black patrons or dancers in taxi dance halls.
291.q: I don't say they would hire them, but it actually looked like segregation, because I've never seen a colored girl work in those places. That's strange.

884.t: Smokey Mary, side-wheel boats and Bucktown camps

690.s: The band played dances on bay boats, meeting at the foot of Dauphin Street.
690.q: Yes, we played all on those bay boats, you know, across, going across on the other side of the Baltimore County. We played dances on those boats quite often. For dancing.

886.t: Dance band with Henry Red Allen and the riverboat

886.q: Simon Phil Mitchell, bass player, he died too. Oh yeah. And Albojack on, Triumph on, Johnny Thomas on the drum. And Leonard Boccaf playing with Vagio. We just get plenty of jobs.

293.t: PWA band and the Pelican job with Tab Smith
293.s: Sat in the huge PWA band, then led a small band at the Pelican for $37 a month, visited by Fate Marable's men and Tab Smith.
293.ch: Orleans Pleasure Club to PWA band
293.q: I learned him how to play the piano, and I got Alvin Francis, and I got a boy by the name of Deli Hoosier to play saxophone, and I played the banjo. And we played there, and we was getting $37 a week. $37 a month. A month? And Sherry Wine was a nickel a trough, and a big glass like that, a nickel.

198.t: Boats and playing alongside other bandleaders
198.s: He says he never played on the riverboats, though he played along with Sim Gisby and others.
198.q: Sitting there for, I played along with Sim Gisby and everybody. Yeah. I never played along with them.

113.s: Bowman sang with him on a two-week Delta Queen trip up the Mississippi from New Orleans to Cincinnati, sponsored by the University of Nebraska.
